details:
Terrestrial Analog Finder (terra-twin-trailblazer)

This is a web app built by Team Pascal’s Blue, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is an interactive 3D globe that scores places on Earth by how closely they resemble the Moon or Mars. Mission teams can use it to find new “terrestrial analog” sites, places where equipment and methods can be tested before flying. Well-known analogs include the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater and Death Valley.

How it works

Each site is described by a normalized (0–1) profile across seven features: aridity, cold, UV/radiation, slope, basaltic geology, fine regolith and impact features. Each feature is labeled with the open dataset it corresponds to, such as ERA5, CHIRPS, WorldClim, Copernicus DEM, LRO LOLA, MGS MOLA, CRISM, HiRISE and LROC. The Moon and Mars each have a reference profile. A site’s score is 100 × (1 − weighted mean absolute difference) between its profile and the chosen target, so a higher score means a closer match. The method has three steps: profile the sites, score them against the targets, then validate against known analogs and rank the new candidates.

Features

  • A 3D globe built with React Three Fiber, with orbit controls, clickable site markers and an Earth / Moon / Mars toggle. Markers are colored and sized by score.
  • A choice of Moon or Mars as the comparison target.
  • Sliders (0–2) for each feature weight, with the ranking updating instantly.
  • Terrain filters (desert, polar, volcanic, impact, cave) and an “only new candidates” switch.
  • A radar chart comparing a selected site with the target profile, plus a ranked list of all sites.
  • A “validation average” that shows how well the scoring rates the known analogs.
  • Moon and Mars modes that show landing sites (Apollo 11 and 17, Jezero, Gale and others) with instrument references.

Data and code

The app includes 22 sites, 12 known analogs and 10 new candidates, including Lonar Crater (India), Holuhraun (Iceland), the Lut Desert (Iran), the Namib Sand Sea, the Danakil Depression, Tso Kar (Ladakh) and Kamil Crater (Egypt). Site profiles are hard-coded and hand-assigned in src/lib/analogs.ts. The README says the features correspond to open datasets, but the code does not pull live data from them.

Tech stack

  • TanStack Start and Router on React 19
  • Vite, with Nitro for deployment
  • three.js and React Three Fiber for the globe
  • Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn/Radix UI components
  • Recharts for the radar chart
  • TypeScript, with Vitest, ESLint and Prettier

The project has a small test suite covering the analog scoring and app routing. It runs with npm install and npm run dev and needs Node 20.19+ or 22.12+.
